newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to sell 41,800 tonnes of rice to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to sell 41,800 tonnes of rice to Iraq.

text.p: Two Pakistani firms have won tenders to supply a total of 41,800 tonnes of rice to the Grain Board of Iraq, dealers said on Thursday.
They said Iraq issued the tender through the Pakistani embassy in Baghdad last week after getting clearance from the UN sanctions committee.
The Pakistani government signed an agreement on October 6 to supply food and other U.N.-approved commodities to Iraq.
Some 36 Pakistani firms took part in the rice tender.
Nabil Enterprises Ltd won a contract to export 15,000 tonnes of IRRI-6 grade rice at $238 CIF per tonne for shipment to Um Qasr port by December 15, one dealer said.
Mahmood (pvt) Ltd will export 26,800 tonnes of IRRI-6 rice at $239.74 a tonne CIF for shipment by the last week of November, he said.
However, dealers said the Iraqi government had yet to spell out how it would pay for the rice.

"The Iraqi government has not clarified how the payments are going to be made," dealer Khalid Ghori of Matco Rice Processing Ltd said. He said the Pakistani and Iraqi governments were expected to sort out the issue in the next few days.
